 COMMON-JUDGMENT

The petitioners in M.V.C.No.7551/2024 &
M.V.C.No.7552/2024 have filed these claim petitions  SCCH-24 3 MVC 7551/2024  C/w  MVC 7552/2024 under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by them in a road traffic accident.
2. These two petitions have arisen out of the same accident.
Therefore as per Clubbing memo dated 13-06- 2025 filed by the counsel for Petitioners, these two petitions have been clubbed together for common evidence and common disposal.

3. The case of the petitioners is as follows:-
 That on 25-05-2024 at about 18-00 hours petitioner Chandan V.V. in M.V.C. No.7551/2024 was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04/KY-2045 along with Pillion rider Sri.Pavan V.S. ie., petitioner in MVC.7552/2024 on service road, Bengaluru - Mangaluru NH-75 road, towards Varahasandra village.
Pavan vs Versus Nanje Gowda on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143446811/

When they reached opposite to Dream Jeeva Dhaba,
Bellur cross, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya Dist., at that time the driver of TATA Intra goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-13/D-0290 came in a rash and negligent manner and taken turn towards service road from NH -75 without giving any signal and dashed to the petitioners vehicle, result of which the petitioners in both the cases fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioners in both the case were shifted to Adi Chunchanagiri Hospital, B.G.Nagar, wherein they took treatment as an inpatient and spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical and other incidental charges.
5. Prior to the accident, the petitioner in MVC.7551/2024 was hale and healthy.
He was doing Agriculture and Milk vending work and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability suffered on account of the grievous injuries he is not in a position to do the work.
He has suffered mental pain and agony.
6. Prior to the accident, the petitioner in MVC.7552/2024 was hale and healthy.
He was doing Agriculture and Milk vending work and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability suffered on account of the grievous injuries he is not in a position to do the work.
He has suffered mental pain and agony.
7. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - the owner of TATA Intra goods vehicle bearing  SCCH-24 5 MVC 7551/2024  C/w  MVC 7552/2024 Reg.No.KA-13/D-0290 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed exparte.

8. The respondent no.2 /the Insurer of TATA Intra goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-13/D-0290 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and Pavan vs Versus Nanje Gowda on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143446811/
3 conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary and proper parties for the adjudication of the above petition and that the jurisdictional police have filed charge sheet even against the rider of the motor cycle bearing reg No.KA-04-KY- 2045 who was not holding valid driving license.
The respondent no.2 further contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid driving license.

9. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
 ISSUES  (in MVC.7551/2024)
 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has  sustained injuries on account of road traffic  accident on 25-05-2024 at about 18-00  hours, opp Dream Jeeva Dhaba on NH-75  SCCH-24 6 MVC 7551/2024  C/w  MVC 7552/2024  service road, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala  Taluk, Mandya District, due to rash and  negligent driving of the driver of Tata Intra  Goods vehicle bearing Reg.no.KA-13-D-  0290?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation as claimed? If so, what is the  quantum?

From whom payable?
 3. What order or Award?

sentences.text: In order to substantiate the contention, the petitioner in MVC No.7551/2024 is examined as PW.1 and Petitioner in MVC No.7552/2024 is examined as PW.2.

The PWs.1 and 2 have specifically deposed in their chief examination that the driver of TATA Intra goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-13/D-0290 (here in after called the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against their motorcycle and caused the accident, result of which they have sustained grievous injuries.
 16.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 and PW.2 have relied upon Ex.P1 to P6 and Ex.P11 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, Crime details form, Vehicle seizure mahazar,
IMV report, Wound Certificate of PW.1, Charge sheet and Wound certificate of PW.2.
 17.
On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sri.Arjun Kumar.
N.S case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.86/2024 of Bellur Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC and U/sec.187 of IMV Act.

SCCH-24 9 MVC 7551/2024  C/w  MVC 7552/2024 The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC and U/sec.187 of IMV Act.
 18.
The complaint is lodged without any delay.

Learned counsel for respondent no.2 has vehemently argued that the accident in question has occurred even due to the negligence of the petitioners hence the petitioners have to forgo compensation to the extent of negligency contributed by them.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that when the left front portion of the offending vehicle and right portion of the motorcycle was damaged it has to be concluded that the petitioners by riding their vehicle in a rash and negligent manner hit to the left door of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: If the charge sheet is perused, the PW.1 is charge sheeted for not holding valid driving license.
The PW.1 was not holding valid driving license and for that reason charge sheet was filed against the PW.1 will not be a ground to hold that PW.1 has also contributed negligence.

When charge sheet is filed against PW.1 for  SCCH-24 10 MVC 7551/2024  C/w  MVC 7552/2024 his not having valid driving license then penal provision would attract against the PW.1.
 20.

If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, it is not in dispute that the motorcycle of the petitioners was proceeding in the service road from Bellur cross towards Varahasandra and offending vehicle which was proceeding in NH -75 from Bangalore towards Mangalore took turn towards service road and hit against the motorcycle.

It is true that there is provision at the spot of accident to take turn towards service road from National High way and accordingly the driver of the offending vehicle entered his vehicle on the service road from the National High way.

The width of the service road at the spot of accident is nearly 28 feet and the accident in question has occurred at a distance of 5 feet from the left edge of service road leads from Bellur cross towards Varahasandra.
When offending vehicle was taking turn towards service road, the driver ought to have taken the turn with all care and caution in slow and steady manner.

It appears that the driver of the offending vehicle without giving any signal took the vehicle towards service road in a rash and negligent manner, hence only the offending vehicle hit to the motorcycle which was proceeding on the left side of the  SCCH-24 11 MVC 7551/2024  C/w  MVC 7552/2024 road.
Admittedly, respondent no.1 who is the owner of the offending vehicle has remained ex-parte and thereby not contested the petition.
The respondent no.2 having contended that the PW.1 has contributed negligence, failed to examine driver of the offending vehicle.

When the left side of the offending vehicle and right side of the motorcycle was damaged which is evident from IMV report, it can be said that the offending vehicle which came from NH -75 suddenly entered the service road and hit to the motorcycle.

Hence, the materials placed on record clearly reveals Pavan vs Versus Nanje Gowda on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143446811/
7 the rash and negligent act on the part of the offending vehicle.
Hence without discussing much on this point this court holds Issue No.1 in both the cases in the Affirmative.
21. Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.7551/2024:- P.W.1 has given evidence to the effect of his sustained severe injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., wound certificate and discharge summary which are at Ex.P.5 and 7.
On going through the medical documents it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient from 25-05-2024 to 03-06- 2024 for a period of 9 days at Aadhichunchanagiri Hospital.

As per the wound certificate issued from  SCCH-24 12 MVC 7551/2024  C/w  MVC 7552/2024 Adhichunchanagiri Hospital, Mandya District to the effect that petitioner has been treated for eight injuries of which injury no.1, 6, 7 and 8 are grievous in nature and injury No.2, 3, 4 and 5 are simple in nature.

Bangalore Rural District is examined as PW.3 and through him Authorization Letter, MLC Extract, Police Intimation, Discharge summary, Inpatient record are marked as Ex.P16 to Ex.P20.

PW.4 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent disability to right arm at 32% and to the whole body at 11% .
24. If the cross examination of PW.4 is carefully perused, PW.4 is not a treated doctor.

Admittedly the PW.1 has taken conservative treatment and no implant  SCCH-24 13 MVC 7551/2024  C/w  MVC 7552/2024 Pavan vs Versus Nanje Gowda on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143446811/

sentences.text: As per the evidence of PW.4 no infection or swelling was found at the time of examination of PW.1 by the PW.4.

It is deposed by PW4 that K-wire was fixed to the wrist of the PW.1 and since it is a simple/closed fracture only conservative treatment was given without advising to take physiotherapy treatment and that PW.1 can do his daily work without any difficulty.

25. When Pw.1 has taken conservative treatment and no implant was fixed and when PW.1 can do his daily work without any difficulty, under such circumstances it can be said that the PW.4 has assessed the disability on higher side as 11% on whole body.

Considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner, and the line of treatment taken by the petitioner it can be said that the petitioner may have suffered disability less than 5% and disability of less than 5% may not come in the way of discharging the work.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head loss of future income due to disability.
At the most for the injuries suffered by the petitioner he may be entitled for compensation under the head of loss discomfort and amenities.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained,
period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
27. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained four grievous injuries and four simple injuries.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering.
28. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner are concerned, he has produced 40 medical bills for Rs.51,317/- as per Ex.P9.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.51,317/-.

The petitioner has sustained four grievous and four simple injuries and has taken treatment for 9 days as inpatient at Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Mandya District.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 2 months as complete laid down period.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
SCCH-24 9 MVC 7551/2024  C/w  MVC 7552/2024 The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC and U/sec.187 of IMV Act.
 18.
If the charge sheet is perused, the PW.1 is charge sheeted for not holding valid driving license.
The PW.1 was not holding valid driving license and for that reason charge sheet was filed against the PW.1 will not be a ground to hold that PW.1 has also contributed negligence.
When charge sheet is filed against PW.1 for  SCCH-24 10 MVC 7551/2024  C/w  MVC 7552/2024 his not having valid driving license then penal provision would attract against the PW.1.
 20.
If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, it is not in dispute that the motorcycle of the petitioners was proceeding in the service road from Bellur cross towards Varahasandra and offending vehicle which was proceeding in NH -75 from Bangalore towards Mangalore took turn towards service road and hit against the motorcycle.
It is true that there is provision at the spot of accident to take turn towards service road from National High way and accordingly the driver of the offending vehicle entered his vehicle on the service road from the National High way.
When offending vehicle was taking turn towards service road, the driver ought to have taken the turn with all care and caution in slow and steady manner.
It appears that the driver of the offending vehicle without giving any signal took the vehicle towards service road in a rash and negligent manner, hence only the offending vehicle hit to the motorcycle which was proceeding on the left side of the  SCCH-24 11 MVC 7551/2024  C/w  MVC 7552/2024 road.
Admittedly, respondent no.1 who is the owner of the offending vehicle has remained ex-parte and thereby not contested the petition.
The respondent no.2 having contended that the PW.1 has contributed negligence, failed to examine driver of the offending vehicle.
When the left side of the offending vehicle and right side of the motorcycle was damaged which is evident from IMV report, it can be said that the offending vehicle which came from NH -75 suddenly entered the service road and hit to the motorcycle.
25. When Pw.1 has taken conservative treatment and no implant was fixed and when PW.1 can do his daily work without any difficulty, under such circumstances it can be said that the PW.4 has assessed the disability on higher side as 11% on whole body.
Considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner, and the line of treatment taken by the petitioner it can be said that the petitioner may have suffered disability less than 5% and disability of less than 5% may not come in the way of discharging the work.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head loss of future income due to disability.
At the most for the injuries suffered by the petitioner he may be entitled for compensation under the head of loss discomfort and amenities.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained,
period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 2 months as complete laid down period.
Hence taking into consideration the avocation of petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation, this court takes the loss of income during laid down period.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.33,000/- (16,500X2) towards loss of income during the laid down period .
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.
Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 2 months as complete laid down period.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.33,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period .
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.30,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
 41.
The petitioner at his age of 18 years has suffered grievous injuries which definitely caused some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life,
hence, he is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.75,000/-.
Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/-
 2. Medical expenses Rs. 66,946/-
 3. Loss of income during laid down Rs. 33,000/-
 period
4 . Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 30,000/-
 charges and nourishing food  & other incidental charges
5. Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs. 75,000/-
C/w  MVC 7552/2024  Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,74,946/- (Rupees Two Lakh Seventy Four Thousand Nine Hundred Forty Six only)
 42.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioners along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered.
43. Issus No.3 in MVC No.7551/2024 and M.V.C.No.7552/2024 :- In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2 in MVC No.7551/2024 and MVC No.7552/2024, finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
C/w  MVC 7552/2024  ORDER
The claim petitions filed by the petitioner in MVC No.7551/2024 and MVC No. 7552/2024 are hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner in MVC No.7551/2024 is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,64,317/- + cost of Rs.1,500/- imposed vide order on IA No.II & III.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.2,65,817/-
(Rupees Two Lakh Sixty Five Thousand Eight Hundred Seventeen only).
A Sum of Rs.2,64,317/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The petitioner in MVC No.7552/2024 is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,74,946/- + cost of Rs.1,500/- imposed vide order on IA No.II & III.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.2,76,446/-
(Rupees Two Lakh Seventy Six Thousand Four Hundred Forty Six only).
C/w MVC 7552/2024 A Sum of Rs.2,74,956/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest at 6% p.a. within 2 months from the date of award.
On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner in M.V.C.No. 7551/2024 shall be deposited in the name of petitioner in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner in M.V.C.No. 7552/2024 shall be deposited in the name of petitioner in any nationalized bank of the Pavan vs Versus Nanje Gowda on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143446811/
14 choice of C/w MVC 7552/2024 petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- each in MVC No.7551/2024 and MVC.7552/2024.
Draw separate awards accordingly.
